title: Ser vs Estar — the two 'to be's
explanation: Portuguese has two verbs for 'to be'. Use SER for identity, origin, profession, and permanent traits (Sou americano). Use ESTAR for temporary states, feelings, and location (Estou cansado, Estou no hotel).

examples.en: I am from the United States. (ser — origin)
I am very happy here. (estar — temporary state)
She is a teacher. (ser — profession)

title: Present tense with tu
pattern: falar: falo, falas, fala, falamos, falam
explanation: In Portugal, informal speech uses TU: tu falas, tu comes, tu vais. Regular -ar verbs: -o (eu), -as (tu), -a (ele/ela), -amos (nós), -am (eles). Use 'o senhor / a senhora' + 3rd person for polite situations.

examples.en: You speak Portuguese very well! (informal)
We speak English too.

examples.jp: O senhor deseja mais alguma coisa?
examples.en: Would you like anything else? (polite)

title: Questions with 'o que é que'
explanation: Yes/no questions use statement word order with rising intonation: 'Falas inglês?' For detail questions, Portugal loves inserting 'é que': 'O que é que queres?' (What do you want?), 'Onde é que fica?' (Where is it?). Question words: o que, onde, quanto, quando, quem, como, porquê.

examples.en: Do you speak English?
What would you like?

examples.jp: Onde é que fica a casa de banho?
examples.en: Where is the bathroom?

title: Polite requests: queria & pode
explanation: 'Queria um café' (I'd like a coffee — imperfect for politeness) is THE way to order in Portugal. 'Pode repetir?' = Can you repeat? 'Posso pagar com cartão?' = Can I pay by card?

examples.en: I'd like a table for two.
Can you repeat, please?
Can I pay with MB Way?

title: Ter — to have (and hunger, age, hurry)
pattern: eu tenho, tu tens, nós temos
explanation: Ter is irregular and everywhere: 'Tenho uma reserva' (I have a reservation). Portugal uses ter where English uses 'to be': tenho fome (I'm hungry), tenho pressa (I'm in a hurry), tenho 40 anos (I'm 40 years old).

examples.en: I have a reservation.
I'm hungry and in a hurry.
Is there Wi-Fi in the room?

title: The future with ir + infinitive
explanation: The everyday future: 'vou' + infinitive, like English 'going to': 'Vou visitar amanhã' (I'm going to visit tomorrow), 'Vais sair às oito?' (Are you going to leave at eight?).

examples.jp: Vou visitar a Torre de Belém.
examples.en: I'm going to visit the Belém Tower.
We're going to leave at eight.

examples.jp: O que é que vais fazer amanhã?
examples.en: What are you going to do tomorrow?

title: Contractions: do, da, no, na
explanation: Prepositions fuse with articles: de+o → do (of the), em+o → no (in the). You'll hear them constantly: 'Sou do Arizona', 'Estou no hotel', 'Vou para a praia'.

examples.en: I'm from Mesa, in Arizona.
The hotel is on the beach.
I'm at the airport.

title: Muito — very / a lot
explanation: Muito does double duty: as an adverb it's 'very' and never changes (muito obrigado). As a quantity it agrees: muito tempo, muita gente. 'Muito prazer' = nice to meet you.

examples.en: Thank you very much!
There were a lot of people at the party.
I'm very hungry.

title: Gostar de — liking things
explanation: 'To like' always takes 'de': 'Gosto de música' (I like music), 'Gostas de dançar?' (Do you like to dance?). Negative: 'Não gosto de acordar cedo'.

examples.jp: Gosto muito de pastel de nata.
examples.en: I really like pastel de nata.
Do you like Portuguese music?

examples.jp: Não gosto de café com açúcar.
examples.en: I don't like coffee with sugar.

title: Numbers & money
explanation: Um and dois change with gender: um café, uma água; dois cafés, duas águas. Prices in Portugal are in euros: 'cinco euros' (€5), 'dois euros e cinquenta' (€2.50).

examples.en: It costs twenty euros.

examples.jp: Uma água e dois cafés, se faz favor.
examples.en: One water and two coffees, please.
That's forty-five euros.

title: Tudo bem — the universal greeting
explanation: 'Tudo bem?' is both 'how are you?' and its own answer ('Tudo!' = all good). Casual check-ins: 'Tudo fixe?' (all cool?), 'Tudo porreiro?' The standard reply is to repeat it, then 'e tu?'.

examples.en: How are you? — Good, and you?
All good here.

title: Se faz favor & the politeness toolkit
pattern: se faz favor / com licença / desculpe
explanation: In Portugal, 'se faz favor' (or the joined 'se faz favor'/'faz favor') is as common as 'por favor'. 'Com licença' = excuse me (to pass). 'Desculpe' = sorry. Men say 'obrigado', women say 'obrigada' — the ending matches the speaker.

examples.en: An espresso, please.

examples.jp: Com licença, onde fica o metro?
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the metro?
Sorry, I didn't understand.

title: Preterite — talking about the past
explanation: Regular preterite: -ar verbs take -ei (eu), -aste (tu), -ou (ele), -ámos (nós): falei, falaste, falou, falámos. -er/-ir: comi/comeste/comeu, parti/partiste/partiu. Irregular stars: fui/foste (ir, ser), fiz/fizeste (fazer), tive/tiveste (ter), disse/disseste (dizer).

examples.en: Yesterday I went to the beach.

examples.jp: O que é que fizeste no fim de semana?
examples.en: What did you do on the weekend?
We ate grilled fish by the sea.

title: Estar a + infinitive — happening now
explanation: THE European Portuguese progressive: estar a + infinitive = 'am doing right now'. 'Estou a procurar apartamento' (I'm looking for an apartment), 'Está a chover' (it's raining). Brazil uses the gerund (-ndo); Portugal uses 'a + infinitive'.

examples.en: I'm loving Portugal!
Are you adapting well?
I'm eating, I'll call you later. (casual)

title: Ter que / Precisar de — obligations
pattern: ter que + inf / precisar de + inf
explanation: 'Tenho que confirmar a consulta' = I have to confirm the appointment. 'Preciso de voltar?' = Do I need to come back? Note: precisar takes 'de' in Portugal.

examples.en: I have to confirm the appointment.
Does it need a prescription?
Do I need a document?

title: Ficar — location, staying, becoming
explanation: Ficar is a Swiss-army verb: location ('Onde fica o metro?' — where is the metro?), staying ('Vou ficar duas semanas'), and becoming ('Fiquei doente' — I got sick, 'Fico contente' — I'm glad).

examples.en: Where is the station (located)?
I'm staying home today.

examples.jp: Fiquei muito contente com a notícia.
examples.en: I was very happy with the news.

title: Reflexive verbs — European placement
explanation: In Portugal the little pronoun goes AFTER the verb in normal statements: 'Exercito-me três vezes por semana', 'Estou a habituar-me', 'Ela chama-se Juliana'. With estar a + infinitive, it hangs on the infinitive: 'Estou a adaptar-me'.

examples.en: I exercise three times a week.

examples.jp: Estou a adaptar-me ao fuso horário.
examples.en: I'm adapting to the time zone.
I go to bed early during the week.

title: Por vs Para
explanation: Rough guide: PARA points forward — destination, purpose, recipient (Vou para a praia, um presente para ti). POR looks at the path — through, by, duration, exchange (andei pelo parque, obrigado por tudo, paguei dez euros por isto).

examples.jp: Vou para o Porto na sexta-feira.
examples.en: I'm going to Porto on Friday.
I walked through downtown yesterday.
Thanks for everything!

title: Saber vs Conhecer — knowing
explanation: SABER = know facts or how to do something ('Sei nadar' — I can swim). CONHECER = be familiar with people/places ('Conheço Lisboa' — I know Lisbon, 'Conheces a Ana?').

examples.en: Do you know where the bank is?
I know a perfect place!
I don't know this neighborhood yet.

title: Já — already, yet, right away
explanation: Já is tiny but mighty: 'Já!' = yes, I have. 'Já experimentaste?' = have you tried yet? 'Já venho' = be right back. Negative: 'ainda não' (not yet).

examples.en: Have you tried ginjinha? — I have!
I haven't been to Belém yet.
I'll send you the location right away.

title: Este, esse, aquele — this & that
explanation: Three distances: ESTE = this (near me), ESSE = that (near you), AQUELE = that over there (far). Everyday neuter forms: isto, isso, aquilo: 'O que é isso?' (what is that?), 'Quanto é isto?' (how much is this?).

examples.en: How much is this?
That restaurant is great.

examples.jp: Aquele prédio alto é o hotel.
examples.en: That tall building over there is the hotel.

title: Queria & gostava — polite wishing
explanation: The imperfect softens requests beautifully: 'Queria marcar uma consulta' (I'd like to book an appointment — the phone-call essential), 'Gostava de jantar convosco' (I'd like to have dinner with you all).

examples.en: I'd like to book an appointment.

examples.jp: Gostava de um café, se faz favor.
examples.en: I'd like a coffee, please.
I'd like a table for two.

title: Imperfect — used to / was -ing
explanation: The imperfect describes habits and backgrounds in the past: 'Trabalhava remotamente' (I used to work remotely), 'Estava a chover' (it was raining), 'Quando era criança' (when I was a kid).

examples.en: I used to work at an American company.
It was very hot yesterday.

examples.jp: Quando era criança, morava no campo.
examples.en: When I was a kid, I lived in the countryside.

title: Há — time expressions
explanation: 'Há quanto tempo?' = for how long? 'Há dez anos' = for ten years. With preterite it means ago: 'Cheguei há dois dias' (I arrived two days ago).

examples.jp: Trabalho nisto há mais de dez anos.
examples.en: I've worked in this for more than ten years.

examples.jp: Há quanto tempo se sente assim?
examples.en: How long have you been feeling like this?
He arrived an hour ago.

title: Casual contractions: 'tou, 'tá, 'tava
explanation: Spoken Portuguese clips 'estar' constantly: 'tou (I am), 'tá (is/are), 'tava (was). ''Tou cansado', ''Tá frio?', ''Tava no metro'. Write formal, speak casual — recognize and use both.

examples.en: I'm hungry, shall we eat?
It's very hot today.

examples.jp: Eu 'tava no metro quando começou a chover.
examples.en: I was on the metro when it started raining.

title: Nós — the real 'we' (not 'a gente')
explanation: In Portugal 'we' is NÓS with full plural endings: 'Nós comemos grelhados' (we ate grilled food), 'Vamos sair às nove'. (The Brazilian shortcut 'a gente' is understood but marks you as Brazilian-sounding.)

examples.en: We're going out at nine.
We met at work.

examples.jp: Ao fim de semana nós descansamos.
examples.en: On the weekend we rest.

title: Subjunctive with espero que
explanation: Hopes about others use the present subjunctive: 'Espero que dê certo' (I hope it works out), 'Espero que melhores' (I hope you get better). Trigger words: espero que, tomara que, quero que.

examples.jp: Espero que o meu português melhore.
examples.en: I hope my Portuguese improves.
I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow!

examples.jp: Quero que conheças a minha família.
examples.en: I want you to meet my family.

title: Diminutives — -inho/-inha
explanation: Portugal shrinks everything too, but with its own flavor: 'um bocadinho' (a tiny bit — you hear it hourly), 'pertinho' (nice and close), 'rapidinho' (real quick), 'um cafezinho' (in the North).

examples.en: I speak a tiny bit of Portuguese.
The pastry shop is right nearby.
I'll go there real quick.

title: Slang — fixe, pá, porreiro
explanation: Core Portuguese slang: 'fixe' = cool/fine (the #1 word), 'porreiro' = cool/nice, 'pá' = man/dude ('Então pá!'), 'podes crer' = you bet, 'giro' = cute/cool, 'brutal' = awesome, 'espetáculo' = great.

examples.en: Hey man, all good? — All good!
The concert was awesome.
Agreed, see you Saturday. You bet!

title: Achar vs Pensar — opinions
explanation: 'Achar' is the everyday opinion verb: 'Acho que sim' (I think so), 'Acho que ele fica' (I think he stays). Negative: 'Acho que não'. 'Pensar' is about deliberating: ''Tou a pensar ir àquele bar'.

examples.jp: O que é que achaste do jogo?
examples.en: What did you think of the game?

examples.jp: Acho que vão despedir o selecionador.
examples.en: I think they'll fire the national coach.

examples.jp: 'Tou a pensar naquele bar com música ao vivo.
examples.en: I'm thinking about that bar with live music.

title: Formal address for elders & family visits
explanation: Meeting Portuguese families: 'o senhor / a senhora' shows respect to the parents' generation, with 3rd-person verbs: 'A senhora quer mais café?' Also: 'está à vontade' (make yourself at home), 'faça favor de entrar' (do come in).

examples.en: Good evening, ma'am. Nice to meet you.

examples.jp: O senhor aceita mais um bocado?
examples.en: Would you like another piece, sir?

examples.jp: Está à vontade, a casa é sua.
examples.en: Make yourself at home, the house is yours.

title: Imperatives — casual commands (tu)
explanation: Casual tu-imperative: 'Conta!' (tell me!), 'Olha!' (look/listen!), 'Descontrai!' (relax!). Reflexives attach: 'Cuida-te!' (take care!). Negative tu commands add -s: 'Não fales!', 'Não esqueças!'.

examples.jp: Conta lá, o que é que aconteceu?
examples.en: Tell me, what happened?
Relax, you're a guest.
Take care! See you next week.

title: Storytelling: 'tava a + infinitive
explanation: Set the scene of a story with the imperfect progressive: 'Eu 'tava no metro quando começou a chover a potes' (I was on the metro when it started pouring). Background = 'tava a + infinitive; interrupting event = preterite.

examples.en: I was sleeping when you called.

examples.jp: Nós estávamos a jantar quando ele chegou.
examples.en: We were having dinner when he arrived.

title: Conditional — seria, gostaria, poderia
explanation: The conditional ('would') is easy: verb + -ia: 'Seria incrível' (it would be amazing), 'Gostaria de jantar convosco' (I'd love to have dinner with you all), 'Podia enviar-me a foto?' (could you send me the photo?).

examples.en: It would be amazing to live in Portugal.
Would you like to have dinner with us?
Could you send me the photo?

title: Fixe, giro, brutal — saying 'cool'
explanation: Portuguese approval words: 'fixe' (cool — the everyday one), 'giro' (nice/cute), 'porreiro' (cool), 'brutal' (awesome), 'espetáculo' (great — 'Foi um espetáculo!'), 'ótimo' (great).

examples.en: Everything's cool here!

examples.jp: A tua casa é muito gira.
examples.en: Your home is really nice.
The party was awesome.

title: Keeping conversation alive
pattern: e tu? / conta lá / a sério? / pois!
explanation: Conversation maintenance kit: 'E tu?' (and you?), 'Conta lá!' (tell me!), 'A sério?' (really?), 'Que giro!' (how cool!), 'Pois!' (yeah! — the universal Portuguese agreement), 'Exato!' (exactly!), 'Então?' (so?/and?). Use them constantly — Portugal runs on these little reactions.

examples.en: You won't believe it! — Tell me!

examples.jp: A sério? Que giro, conta-me tudo.
examples.en: Really? How cool, tell me everything.
— I liked it a lot. — Yeah, me too.
